\[
\big(a_J,\ (h_j, v_j, d_j)_{j=1}^{J}\big) = \operatorname{DWT}(I),
\quad
\hat{I} = \operatorname{IDWT}\big(a_J,\ \eta_T(h_j),\ \eta_T(v_j),\ \eta_T(d_j)\big),
\qquad
\eta_T(w) = \begin{cases}
  \operatorname{sign}(w)\, \max(|w| - T,\ 0) & \text{soft} \\
  w\, [\,|w| \ge T\,] & \text{hard}
\end{cases}
\qquad
T = \begin{cases}
  \sigma \sqrt{2 \ln N} & \text{VisuShrink} \\
  \sigma^2 / \sigma_{x,b} & \text{BayesShrink} \\
  \sigma\, t^{S}_b & \text{SureShrink}
\end{cases}
\qquad
\hat{\sigma} = \frac{\operatorname{median}(|d_1|)}{0.6745},
\quad
J = 3
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): The input channel
- \(a_J\): The approximation after J levels
- \(h_j, v_j, d_j\): The horizontal, vertical and diagonal details of level j. Level 1 is the finest.
- \(w\): One detail coefficient
- \(\eta_T\): The shrink rule with threshold T
- \(T\): The threshold, in pixel values
- \(\sigma\): The standard deviation of the noise
- \(N\): The number of pixels
- \(n_b, \sigma_{x,b}\): The number of coefficients in subband b, and the estimated deviation of the signal in it
- \(t^{S}_b\): The SURE threshold of subband b in units of sigma

The discrete wavelet transform splits the image into a coarse approximation a_J and, at each level j, horizontal, vertical and diagonal details. An orthogonal wavelet transform turns white Gaussian noise of standard deviation sigma into white noise of the same sigma in every subband, away from the image borders. Edges and textures make a few large coefficients. So small coefficients are mostly noise. The shrink rule eta_T sets them to 0. When sigma is 0, it is estimated from the diagonal details d_1 of the finest level. The estimate is their median absolute value divided by 0.6745, the 75th percentile of the standard normal distribution. Coefficients that are exactly 0 are left out. VisuShrink uses the universal threshold of Donoho and Johnstone, where N is the number of pixels. BayesShrink, after Chang, Yu and Vetterli, divides sigma^2 by the signal deviation sigma_x,b of each subband b. That is the square root of the subband variance minus sigma^2. If the difference is not positive, the subband is set to 0. SureShrink, after Donoho and Johnstone, picks a threshold t^S_b for each subband, in units of sigma. It minimizes Stein's unbiased risk estimate of soft thresholding, from 0 to sqrt(2 ln n_b). A sparse subband gets the universal threshold of its size instead. The approximation a_J is kept.
